title: Change Employers for Career Progress, Workers Say
paragraphs: If you wanted to move forward in your career, would you look for opportunities at your current company, or start looking elsewhere?
A new survey of more than 2,000 workers across the US and UK has found that 66% think they would need to leave their current employer to advance their career.

The survey, done by Propeller Insights for workplace assessment company SHL, found that many employees want to learn new skills and move into new roles — but do not always have opportunities to do so where they already work.
One problem may be that employers don't have a full picture of what their workers can do.
Only two in five workers said their manager understands the skills they have beyond those needed for their current job. And 89% said they would take a skills assessment to show what they can do.

Many employees also think companies are more interested in bringing in people from outside. Fifty-nine percent of US workers and 49% of UK workers said their employer prefers this to helping current staff move into new jobs.
Managers may also get in the way. Nearly a third of workers said their manager not wanting to lose a good employee was one of the main things stopping them from changing roles.
At the same time, 84% said they want employers to help them find opportunities within the company that match their skills and experience.
Learning new skills is also very important for many workers. More than 40% said the skills they would gain were more important than job title when considering a new job offer.
And more than eight in 10 said they would retrain to get a higher-level job, while a similar share would retrain to move into a different type of job.
